text:
maria: Heads up — apiserver p95 for GET /api/v1/namespaces jumped to ~800ms in us-west1 at 09:12 UTC. Seeing lots of client retries.
raj: I see the alert. api-server error rate + retry count spiking in the dashboard.
james: KV IOPS on etcd nodes spiked ~3x around the same time, sustained for ~2m. Possible compaction or backup overlap?
elena: controller-manager logs show ScaleUp loop requeues, many Pending pods waiting for GPU nodes. Pod create rates surged.
maria: repro snippet from the apiserver logs (truncated):
```
E0907 09:12:23.487] apiserver: read tcp 10.0.1.5:443->10.0.2.9:59876: i/o timeout
W0907 09:12:24.012] request "GET /api/v1/namespaces" took 0.79s, retries=3
```
raj: etcd metrics: commit_durations_p50 ~ 12ms -> 120ms, p95 -> 900ms. leader_cpu ~ 85%.
james: I can see two short etcd leader elections at 09:11:50 and 09:12:18 in the audit logs. That would explain KV stalls.
elena: GPU provisioner backlog grew from 8 -> 72 pending gpu pods in ~90s, controller-manager backlog queue depth jumped. Looks correlated.
maria: Ops-automate reported a scheduled snapshot job starting at 09:11:45 for the etcd cluster in us-west1. Could be causing IO bursts. @ops-automate can you confirm? :eyes:
ops-automate: snapshot job etcd-usw1-snap-2026-09-07 started, duration 46s, wrote ~3GB to disk. No errors.
raj: If snapshot beats with compaction/sync, IO latency spike can cause leader election if timeouts cross. We should throttle snapshot IO or move to off-hours.
james: Short-term: bump apiserver etcd dial timeout and increase apiserver keepalive? That reduces client retries but masks root cause.
elena: Also the GPU pools are over-provisioned bursting into Kube autoscaler — cost concern. If controller-manager gets delayed it keeps requeueing pods which increases API load. Vicious cycle.
maria: Proposal: 1) pause scheduled etcd snapshot jobs for 30m in us-west1, 2) add a soft IO throttle to snapshotter, 3) increase apiserver etcd timeout from 5s -> 8s for the region, 4) investigate reserving a small dedicated GPU buffer to avoid mass scheduling at once. Thoughts?
raj: +1 to pausing snapshot. Also add alerting for snapshot I/O duration > 30s.
james: For longer term: move snapshot writes to a different disk or use streaming backups to object store to reduce host iops. Also consider leader affinity across hosts.
elena: On GPU reserve: we could set a small pool of reserved nodes (spot + reserved) so burst doesn't hit controller-manager all at once. That will cost some baseline $$ but prevent spikes. I'll run numbers.
maria: Can someone run the quick mitigation: pause snapshot in usw, bump apiserver timeout, and flip the retain flag on provisioner to keep 10 GPUs warm? Who can take?
elena: I'll take the provisioner warm-up (will open PR to config and patch autoscaler). ETA 20m.
raj: I'll patch the apiserver etcd dial timeout for the usw cluster now (rolling patch) and add temporary alert.
james: I'll disable the snapshot job and schedule it for +3h. Will also collect iostat from etcd hosts and attach.
ops-automate: snapshot job paused: etcd-usw1-snap-2026-09-07 paused by james at 09:18 UTC.
maria: Thanks team. After actions, p95 dropped back to ~120ms and Pending GPU pods fell to 14 in 7m. Will monitor for the next 30m.
raj: Noted improvement in etcd commit_p95 -> 60ms, leader CPU down to ~55%.
elena: Provisioner warm pool change applied. Reserving 10 GPUs across 2 AZs. Cost delta estimate ~+$4.2k/month.
james: Attached iostat excerpt showing write latency spike on etcd host osv-etc1: 
```
Device: rbd0 tps=430 read/s=12 write/s=410 r_await=1.2 w_await=315.4 svctm=0.24
```
maria: Filing follow-up: create runbook entry for "etcd snapshot IO -> apiserver retry storm" and add to postmortem if we see recurrence. For now monitoring looks stable. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: Incident created INC-2026-418: apiserver-read-retry-kvburst-usw1. Assigned: eng-sre.
maria: closing loop — will leave thread open for 1h for observations.
